name: Naxalite-Maoist insurgency (India)
started: 1967 (Naxalbari uprising); current phase is the final government offensive of 2024-2026
summary: India declared victory over its decades-old Maoist insurgency on 30 March 2026, after a two-year offensive killed the movement's top leader and pushed thousands to surrender. Violence has fallen to a trickle, though two senior commanders remain at large and vowed to keep fighting.

sides.name: Government of India and state governments
Communist Party of India (Maoist)
leaders: Two senior commanders reported at large after Mar 2026 (names not given in source)
sides.strength: Residual; affected area shrank to three districts by early 2026 (Wikipedia).

background: The Maoist insurgency once spread across a 'Red Corridor' of forested tribal districts in central and eastern India. A sustained offensive in Chhattisgarh's Bastar region killed CPI (Maoist) general secretary Nambala Keshava Rao and 26 others on 21 May 2025, and Home Minister Amit Shah set a 31 March 2026 deadline to end the insurgency. This matters because the campaign is a test of whether a heavy security approach can end a rural insurgency rooted in land and mining disputes; critics say the crackdown has extended to treating urban dissent as insurgency.
year: Fatalities fell from 477 in 2025 (390 of them Maoists) to 39 in 2026 by the time of the latest data compiled (37 Maoists, 2 civilians, no security forces). In February 2026 Amit Shah vowed the insurgency would end by March, and on 30 March India declared it over; Chhattisgarh's Vijay Sharma said all insurgents had been killed or had surrendered except two commanders, who pledged to fight on. In September a special NIA court convicted and sentenced to death ten accused in the 2013 Darbha valley attack.
situation: As of late October 2026 the insurgency is residual, concentrated in remnants in the Bastar forests; the state is now focused on prosecutions and on development schemes in former insurgent areas.
technical: SATP data (via Wikipedia): 2025: 141 fatal incidents, 477 deaths (54 civilians, 33 security forces, 390 Maoists); 2026 to page cutoff: 8 fatal incidents, 39 deaths.
Affected zone shrank to 3 districts by early 2026, from 38 districts in 2024 (Wikipedia).
CPI (Maoist) general secretary Nambala Keshava Rao killed 21 May 2025 with 26 others (Wikipedia).
More than 10,000 Maoists surrendered between 2015 and 2025 (Wikipedia).
casualties: 39 deaths in 2026 to the latest compiled date; 477 in 2025 (SATP via Wikipedia).

timeline.event: India declares the Naxalite insurgency ended.
Ten accused in the 2013 Darbha valley attack sentenced to death.

outlook: Watch whether the two remaining senior commanders regroup cadres, and whether violence spikes around mining projects in tribal areas.

zones.name: Bastar region (Bijapur, Sukma, Narayanpur)
zones.note: Last Maoist stronghold in Chhattisgarh's forests.
